title: Fowler and Hellebuyck lead a week that kept pulling the chances apart from the scores
dek: A Kings win that the numbers loved, a Columbus steal, and an Oilers trio finishing at a pace that rarely lasts.
text:
The most interesting story of the week was a game that did not feel like a hockey game at all. On October 29, Los Angeles beat Ottawa 6-5 in overtime, with Artemi Panarin the star. The Kings generated 5.62 expected goals (a measure of the quality of the chances) to Ottawa's 2.71, which means that in 86% of simulated replays of every shot, Los Angeles wins. Among the goals was a tip-in from Trevor Moore that our model gave a 0.9% chance of going in, the least likely goal of the week. Ottawa scored five and still lost, and Drake Batherson, who had the week's best scoring line, was part of that story.

## Who the league was talking about

Connor Hellebuyck topped the headline count, with 43 stories from 16 outlets in the last five days, now as a New Jersey Devil. As Jesse Granger of The Athletic posted, "Connor Hellebuyck improves to 2-0-0 as a Devil" after New Jersey beat Vegas 5-2. We have only those two games to go on, so we'll leave it there.

Connor McDavid drew the same number of headlines from more outlets (24), and Edmonton's 4-0 win over Calgary produced The Times of India's piece on why he said Tristan Jarry "played great." Matthew Schaefer is getting the same kind of attention on Long Island, where Newsday ran "Islanders' Matthew Schaefer is bigger, stronger, faster and better." Gavin McKenna, in Toronto, is drawing comparisons of his own, including NHL Trade Talk's "McKenna Is Closing the Gap on Caufield in One Surprising Way."

Then there is Jacob Fowler, and here the talk and the numbers agree. TSN asked "How high is Jacob Fowler's ceiling?" Our numbers say the week was real: in two games for Montreal he faced 80 shots, allowed one goal, and saved 6.8 goals more than an average goalie would have against those shots (goals saved above expected), a .988 save percentage. Montreal has won four straight, though the skaters only had 52% of the expected goals, and the goaltending has saved 8.0 goals above expected during the run. Credit the goalie first.

## Best, strangest and most one-sided

Columbus took the week's biggest steal. The Blue Jackets beat Philadelphia 4-3 in overtime on October 27, with Kent Johnson the star, despite 2.1 expected goals to Philadelphia's 4.02. Columbus deserved to win in only 19% of replays. The most lopsided game went the other way, as New Jersey beat Los Angeles 3-1 on October 24, with Arseny Gritsyuk the star and an 81% deserved-to-win mark for the Devils.

The other strange one was Tyson Foerster's shorthanded wrist shot against Anaheim, a 1.3% chance that went in.

## Who owned the week

Five players got hat tricks: Anton Lundell (FLA), Tage Thompson (BUF), Logan Cooley (UTA), Viktor Arvidsson (DET) and Batherson (OTT). Batherson also led the scoring with eight points in three games, tied with Calgary's Joel Farabee and Matt Coronato at eight. His four goals came on 1.5 expected, so some of that will come back down. Filip Forsberg (NSH) had seven points, Kirill Kaprizov (MIN) had seven on 2.9 expected goals, a better match.

At the other end, Philipp Grubauer of Seattle had the rough week in net: eight goals allowed on 35 shots, a .771 save percentage, 4.8 goals worse than expected. On the skater side, Alex Laferriere and Adrian Kempe of Los Angeles each went four games without a goal despite 2.3 and 1.9 expected goals, and Winnipeg's Mark Scheifele had 1.9 with none.

## Up and down

Washington, Carolina and Florida each went 3-0-0 and took 58% to 59% of the expected goals. Carolina leads the league at 11-2-2 and 24 points. Winnipeg went 0-4-0, outscored 18-8, and is winless in eight (0-6-2), outscored 30-16. With 44% of the expected goals, the chances say it's real. Philadelphia went 0-2-1 and sits at 3-8-4, only ahead of Chicago and Vancouver.

## Cooling and warming

Early-season caveat: teams have played about 13 games, and goals settle slower than chances. Three Oilers look hot on the numbers. Evan Bouchard has seven goals on 2.5 expected, Leon Draisaitl 12 on 7.2, and McDavid eight on 5.5. Their finishing rates (18%, 25% and 24%) are well above last season's, and rarely last. McDavid also has a 13-game point streak (8 goals, 28 assists). Pavel Dorofeyev (NYR) is the other way: three goals on 6.7 expected.

## Milestones and moves

Brayden Schenn and William Nylander each reached 300 career goals. Auston Matthews hit 800 career points, Brian Dumoulin played his 800th game and Brayden McNabb his 900th. On October 25, the Rangers agreed to terms with goalie James Reimer on a one-year contract, and Carolina did the same with Alexander Nikishin.
